title: Tower Defense
description: Build a three-lane tower-defense game in Scratch 3, then use its working parts to make another level. This self-guided course is for advanced-beginner preteens: you know basic Scratch blocks, but lists, clones, and My Blocks can be new. Build and test one small part at a time.
objectives: Build towers, defeat enemies, earn coins, and protect a base.
Use two short lists to keep track of six reusable shots.
Give clones their own lane and build-spot numbers.
Use My Blocks to keep useful tasks together.
Make a second level by changing settings instead of copying the game scripts.
Design, playtest, and explain a level of your own.
prerequisites: You can connect blocks, use repeat and if blocks, and create a variable.
You can rename sprites and draw or edit simple costumes.
You do not need previous experience with lists, clones, or My Blocks.
requirements: Use Scratch 3 in a modern desktop browser or the Scratch desktop app.
Work through the chapters in order, keeping a separate saved project at each checkpoint.
Use the exact names shown for sprites, messages, variables, lists, costumes, and My Blocks.
Keep costumes centered and within the given sizes so the position checks match the artwork.
Use the green flag to restart the whole game. Start Wave and Next Level have different jobs.

vocabulary.meaning: One horizontal road that enemies follow toward your base.
A group of enemies that starts when the player clicks Start Wave.
A battlefield challenge containing one or more waves. A new level starts with fresh towers, coins, and base health.
A numbered collection of values. Item 1 in each shot list belongs to build spot 1.
A block you name and define for a useful task on one sprite or the Stage. Calling it runs the blocks under its define block.
A temporary copy of a sprite. Variables made For this sprite only give each clone its own values.
A value that says what the game is doing, such as ready, combat, or lost. Scripts check it before acting.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Defend One Lane
objectives: Draw a clear battlefield and a centered enemy.
Move one enemy using a message from the Stage.
Take one health point when that enemy reaches the base.

steps.title: Picture the Defense
steps.explanation: Enemies enter from the right. Your base is on the left. Towers beside each road shoot along it, but do not block enemies. We will get one road working before expanding the game.
instructions: Start a blank Scratch project and delete the Cat.
Sketch three horizontal roads with a base on their left ends.
Mark two tower spots beside each road, near its left end: one above the road and one below it.
Trace what happens when an enemy is defeated: the player earns coins.
Trace what happens when an enemy gets through: the base loses health.
hints: A tower never needs its own health in this game.

checkpoint.task: Explain the route and the two possible outcomes for an enemy.
checkpoint.expectedResult: You can point to the entrance, base, and build spots and explain coins and base health.
completeWhen: Your sketch has three roads and six tower spots.
Enemies pass the towers rather than stopping to attack them.

steps.title: Draw the Battlefield
steps.explanation: Coordinates give the game a shared map. The three road centers are y 90, y 0, and y -90. We will use the top road first. Simple shapes make positions easy to check.
instructions: Select the Stage and rename its blank backdrop `Battlefield`.
Draw three horizontal roads centered at y 90, y 0, and y -90. Keep the top and bottom edges free for displays and buttons.
Draw a base boundary at x -210. Enemies will enter at x 220.
Paint a sprite named `Enemy` with one costume named `Enemy`.
Center Enemy's rectangle on the costume center mark. Keep it no larger than 24 pixels wide and 20 pixels high, and use size 100.
On Enemy, enter x 220 and y 90 in the sprite position fields. Check that its center sits on the top road.
Create `Base Health` and `Game State` with `For all sprites`.
Show the Base Health and Game State displays while testing this chapter.
hints: X changes left-to-right position; y changes height.
Use the costume editor's center mark, not just the center of the visible paint area.

debuggingTips.symptom: The enemy looks offset from its coordinates.
checks: Select its artwork in Costumes and center it on the costume center mark.
Check that the sprite's size is 100.

checkpoint.task: Place Enemy at x 220, y 90.
checkpoint.expectedResult: The enemy is centered at the right end of the top road.
completeWhen: The road centers use the three specified y values.
Enemy fits inside the 24 by 20 pixel box.

steps.title: Move in Small Steps
steps.explanation: The Stage sends `Enemy Step` to ask Enemy to move once. Using `broadcast and wait` lets that receiving script finish before the Stage continues. Later, the Stage will use this order to move shots before enemies check for hits.
instructions: On the Stage, add the green-flag script below. Create the message `Prepare Enemy` from the first broadcast block's New message option.
Create `Enemy Step` from the broadcast inside the forever loop. Use `broadcast and wait` for both messages.
On Enemy, add `when I receive Prepare Enemy`, followed by `go to x: 220 y: 90` and `show`.
Add Enemy's `when I receive Enemy Step` script. Put `change x by -2` inside `if Game State = combat`.
Inside that same if, after movement, add `if x position < -209`.
Inside this second if, put `change Base Health by -1`, `set Game State to ready`, and `hide`, in that order.
Click the green flag. Wait for the enemy to reach the base. Check that health changes from 5 to 4 only once.
hints: Game State is resetting during setup, combat while Enemy moves, and ready after it finishes. The movement script checks for combat before acting.
Put the smaller if inside the larger if. The outer check stops movement after Game State becomes ready.
The wait belongs on the Stage, outside the if but inside forever. Do not put forever under either Enemy message.

checks: Set Game State to ready when the enemy escapes.
Keep movement and the escape check inside if Game State = combat.

checks: Check that the Stage uses Enemy Step and the Enemy receives the same message.
Prepare Enemy must finish; it must not contain forever.

checkpoint.task: Watch one enemy escape, then wait a little longer.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Enemy hides at the base, Base Health stays at 4, and Game State says ready.
completeWhen: The enemy moves left smoothly.
Health drops once, not repeatedly.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Buy One Tower
objectives: Spend coins by clicking a build spot.
Keep a useful task together in a My Block.
Prevent buying the same tower twice.

steps.title: An Empty Spot and a Built Tower
steps.explanation: One sprite can look like an empty build spot or a tower. Its Built variable remembers which it is. Looking at its costume is useful for the player, but the code will check the variable.
instructions: Load your Chapter 1 project and paint a new sprite named `Tower`.
Give it a centered costume named `Empty`: a small circle or outlined square no larger than 28 by 24 pixels.
Add a visibly different centered costume named `Built`, within the same 28 by 24 pixel limit. A filled rectangle works well.
Make `Coins` with `For all sprites` and show its display.
Drag the Coins display to the top-right of the Stage so it does not cover a build spot.
On Battlefield, add a readable bottom-left label: Click an empty spot. Tower: 30 coins.
Add a second short line: Need 30 coins; built spots cannot be bought again. Keep both lines left of x 0 and clear of the tower spots so later buttons fit on the right.
On Tower, make `Built` with `For this sprite only`. Its value will be 0 for empty and 1 for built.
Add Tower's Prepare Tower script below, creating that message in its event menu.
hints: A costume and a variable can both be named Built. The costume controls appearance; the variable stores a number.

debuggingTips.symptom: The spot appears on the road instead of beside it.
checks: Use x -155 and y 112. The top road is y 90, so this spot is 22 pixels above it.

checkpoint.task: Click Tower's Prepare Tower script in the Code area.
checkpoint.expectedResult: An empty spot appears above the top lane and Built is 0.
completeWhen: The two costumes look different.
Built was made For this sprite only on Tower.

steps.title: Make a Block for Buying
steps.explanation: A My Block gives a task a name. Try to build will check the rules, spend coins, and change the spot into a tower. Keeping those blocks together makes the same task easy to reuse later.
instructions: Select Tower, open My Blocks, and click Make a Block. Name it `Try to build` with no inputs.
Tick `Run without screen refresh` and click OK. We use this only for this short task with no waits: finish the checks and purchase before another click can spend the same coins.
Under `define Try to build`, add an if containing an or: Game State equals ready OR Game State equals combat.
Inside that if, add another if with an `and` block. Put `Built = 0` in its left side.
Put a `not` block in the right side of the and, then put `Coins < 30` inside not. Both halves of the and must be true; not less than 30 lets exactly 30 coins buy a tower.
Inside the inner if, change Coins by -30, set Built to 1, and switch costume to Built, in that order.
Add a separate `when this sprite clicked` script. Attach the new `Try to build` block from the My Blocks category.
Do not put a wait, glide, broadcast, or timed say block inside Try to build.
hints: The define block explains the task; the smaller Try to build block calls it.
The My Block belongs to Tower. You will not find it in the Stage's My Blocks category.

debuggingTips.symptom: The purchase works only with more than 30 coins.
checks: Use not Coins less than 30, rather than Coins greater than 30.

debuggingTips.symptom: Every click charges another 30 coins.
checks: Keep the Built equals 0 check around the purchase.
Set Built to 1 immediately after deducting coins.

checkpoint.task: Explain the purchase checks before running them.
checkpoint.expectedResult: The tower can be bought only while building is allowed, while the spot is empty, and with at least 30 coins.
completeWhen: Both if blocks are nested as shown.
The click script calls the My Block rather than duplicating its contents.

steps.title: Test the Price and the Second Click
steps.explanation: A useful test includes the edge of a rule. Exactly 30 coins should work; 29 should not. Clicking an occupied spot should never spend more coins.
instructions: On the Stage, keep the existing green-flag script. Insert `set Coins to 90` after set Base Health to 5.
Insert `broadcast Prepare Tower and wait` after Prepare Enemy and wait, before Game State becomes combat. Leave the movement loop unchanged.
Click the green flag and buy the tower. Coins should change from 90 to 60; clicking it again should leave 60.
Let the enemy escape. Restart and wait until it escapes again, so Game State is ready and the tower is still empty.
For a temporary test, drag out set Coins to 29 on the Stage and click it. Click the empty tower: it must stay empty with 29 coins.
Change the temporary block to set Coins to 30, click it, and try again. The tower should appear and Coins should become 0.
Delete the temporary set block. Restart and check that Coins returns to 90 and the spot is empty.
hints: The tower does not shoot yet. That is the next chapter.
Test both while the enemy moves and after it escapes: purchases are allowed in combat and ready.

debuggingTips.symptom: The tower stays built after restart.
checks: The Stage must broadcast Prepare Tower and wait before combat.
Tower must set Built to 0 and switch to Empty in that receiver.

checkpoint.task: Pass the 29-coin, 30-coin, repeated-click, and restart tests.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Only an affordable first purchase changes coins. Restart restores an empty spot and 90 coins.
completeWhen: Exactly 30 coins works.
A second click does not charge.
The temporary set block is deleted.

steps.title: Checkpoint: A Tower You Can Buy

checkpoint.expectedResult: The first purchase leaves 60 coins, repeated clicks leave 60, and restart returns to 90.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Make One Shot Work
objectives: Read and replace one item in a list.
Launch, move, miss, and reuse one shot.
Give an enemy two health points and award coins once.

steps.title: Two Lists, One Numbered Shot
steps.explanation: Each tower will eventually have a numbered shot. For now there is only shot 1. Shot X stores its position. Shot Active stores 1 while it is flying and 0 when it is available. A list is like a variable with numbered items.
instructions: Load Chapter 2. In Variables, click Make a List and create `Shot X` with `For all sprites`.
Create the list `Shot Active` with `For all sprites` too.
On the Stage, insert `delete all of Shot X` after `set Game State to resetting`. Attach `add 0 to Shot X` immediately after it.
After those two blocks, attach `delete all of Shot Active`, followed by `add 0 to Shot Active`.
Click the green flag. Show both lists temporarily and check that each contains exactly one item, numbered 1, with value 0.
Click the flag again. Each list must still contain one item, not two. Deleting the old items makes restart predictable.
On Tower, create `ID` with `For this sprite only`.
Insert `set ID to 1` immediately below Tower's `when I receive Prepare Tower` block.
Paint a centered 6 by 6 pixel sprite named `Shot`, with one costume named `Shot`.
On Shot, create its own `ID` with `For this sprite only`.
On Shot, add `when I receive Prepare Shot`. Create `Prepare Shot` in that event's menu, then attach `set ID to 1` and `hide`.
On the Stage, insert `broadcast Prepare Shot and wait` after Prepare Tower and wait, before Game State becomes combat.
hints: Both sprites have an ID variable, but they are separate because each was made For this sprite only.
Replace item changes an existing item. Add makes the list longer. Use add only during setup.

debuggingTips.symptom: A list grows every time the flag is clicked.
checks: Delete all of that list before adding its starting item.

checkpoint.task: Restart twice and check that each list still has one item with value 0.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Both lists have one zero, and Tower and Shot each have their own ID set to 1.
completeWhen: Both list lengths remain 1.
Shot is hidden after preparation.

finishedCode.target: New Stage setup blocks, after Game State becomes resetting
finishedCode.code:

add (0) to [Shot X v]

hide

steps.title: Launch, Move, and Reuse
steps.explanation: Tower changes the list values. Shot reads them and draws the shot. This means the position used for hitting an enemy will be the same position used for showing the shot.
instructions: On Tower, make a My Block named `Update my shot`, with no inputs and Run without screen refresh selected. Keep it short, with no waits or broadcasts.
Build the definition below. Put every check inside if Built equals 1.
First, if this shot is active and its x position is greater than 230, replace its active item with 0. It missed and can be reused.
Next, if its active item is 0, replace its x item with -135 and its active item with 1. This launches at the lane's firing point.
After those checks, replace its x item with its current value plus 10. A newly launched shot moves on this step too.
Add when I receive Tower Step and call Update my shot. Create Tower Step in that event menu.
On Shot, add the Draw Shots script below. It reads the two lists, shows an active shot on y 90 during combat, and otherwise hides.
On the Stage, insert `broadcast Tower Step and wait` immediately before `broadcast Enemy Step and wait`, inside the combat if.
After the combat if, but before the 0.03-second wait, add `broadcast Draw Shots and wait`.
Restart and buy the tower. At this step shots pass through enemies: watch a shot disappear near the right edge and a new shot begin at the firing point.
hints: Drag Tower's round ID block into each item-number input. Do not type the word ID into that input.
Put item ID of Shot X into the left side of the plus block, and type 10 on the right.
Keep Draw Shots outside the combat if so a final shot also hides when combat ends.

debuggingTips.symptom: The shot never moves past its starting point.
checks: Only launch when the active item is 0.
The final replace item must use the current x value plus 10, not just 10.

debuggingTips.symptom: Nothing appears despite changing list values.
checks: The Stage must send Draw Shots each loop.
Shot's ID must be 1 and Game State must be combat.

checkpoint.task: Watch a missed shot and its replacement before adding damage.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Only one shot is visible, and it travels from the left toward the right along the top road.
completeWhen: The list stays one item long.
A missed shot is reused.
Shots currently pass through the enemy; damage comes next.

else

end

steps.title: Check a Shot by Number
steps.explanation: A shot must count only once. Enemy will mark it as used before taking damage. We will put the check in a My Block with an input, so later we can ask the same block to check shot 1 or shot 2.
instructions: On Enemy, create `HP` with `For this sprite only`. HP means the enemy's remaining health points; each enemy will need its own value.
Insert `set HP to 2` immediately below `when I receive Prepare Enemy`.
Open My Blocks and click Make a Block. Type `Check shot` as its name.
Click Add an input number or text and name the input `slot`.
Select `Run without screen refresh` and click OK.
Build the Check shot definition below. Drag the round slot input from its define block into the list item inputs. Do not make a variable named slot.
Under define Check shot, add an if with `HP > 0` as its condition.
Inside that if, add another if: item slot of Shot Active equals 1.
Inside that, put the position check shown below. Its two halves are joined by and, and each half has a not around its comparison.
Inside the position check, first replace item slot of Shot Active with 0, then change HP by -1. Do not put a wait between them.
Read the position example in the next step before connecting this block to Enemy Step.
hints: Slot is an input to this call, not a new shared variable.
A hit marks the shot inactive before another enemy could use it. Hiding Shot by itself would not change the list.
If HP reaches 0, later calls do nothing, so a defeated enemy will not use another shot.

debuggingTips.symptom: The input slot appears as plain text inside a list block.
checks: Drag the rounded slot block out of the define block and into the item-number input.

checkpoint.task: Trace a successful call to Check shot 1.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Shot Active item 1 changes to 0 before HP falls from 2 to 1.
completeWhen: The input is a round block, not typed text.
The shot is marked used before damage.
No wait or broadcast is inside this definition.

define Check shot (slot)
if <(HP) > (0)> then
  if <(item (slot) of [Shot Active v]) = (1)> then
    if <<not <(item (slot) of [Shot X v]) < ((x position) - (12))>> and <not <((item (slot) of [Shot X v]) - (10)) > ((x position) + (14))>>> then
      replace item (slot) of [Shot Active v] with (0)
      change [HP v] by (-1)
    end
  end
end

steps.title: Why Check Two Positions?
steps.explanation: The enemy moves left 2 pixels while the shot moves right 10. They can cross between two displayed positions. Our comparisons check that movement using the shot's center and an enemy half-width of 12.
instructions: Draw an enemy center at x 100. Its current left edge is 88, because 100 minus 12 is 88.
Write its previous center at 102. Its previous right edge was 114: 102 plus 12.
Try a shot whose current x is 90. Its previous x was 80. The current shot is not left of 88, and its previous position is not right of 114: a hit.
Try a shot whose current x is 70. It has not reached 88 yet: no hit.
Try a shot whose current x is 130. Its previous x was 120, already beyond 114: no hit.
Match 12, 10, and 14 in your Check shot block to the enemy half-width, shot movement, and previous enemy edge. Keep the movement speeds fixed in this course.
Now draw two enemies overlapping at x 100, each with HP 2. Give shot 1 an x value of 90 and an active value of 1.
Trace the first enemy's Check shot 1 call: the position check passes, Shot Active item 1 becomes 0, then that enemy's HP becomes 1.
Trace the other enemy's call: the active item is already 0, so its HP stays 2. One shot caused only one damage event. Scratch may check either enemy first; our game does not promise which one.
hints: The Sensing block `touching [Shot]?` checks whether the costumes touch at their current positions. This game uses the positions in Shot X instead, so it can check a crossing between moves before Shot draws its new position.
Not less than includes equality. Not greater than also includes equality.
You are checking a small movement that happened during this update, not searching the whole road for an enemy.

debuggingTips.symptom: Every enemy is hit as soon as a shot appears.
checks: The two comparisons must be joined by and, not or.
Check the nesting of not and each comparison against the code panel.

checkpoint.task: Explain the three shot examples using your drawing.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Shot x 90 hits the enemy at 100; shots at 70 and 130 do not.
completeWhen: You can identify the current and previous shot positions.
You have kept shot movement at 10 and enemy movement at -2.

steps.title: Two Hits and One Reward
steps.explanation: Enemy now uses its HP to decide whether it was defeated. A defeated enemy earns coins. An escaped enemy damages the base. Only one of those outcomes should happen.
instructions: On Enemy, replace the earlier Enemy Step script with the version below. Keep Prepare Enemy and the Check shot definition.
After moving left by 2, call Check shot with input 1.
Use if HP less than 1 then else. In the first branch, add 10 coins, set Game State to ready, and hide.
Inside else, put the original escape check. It still removes one base health, sets ready, and hides.
Restart and buy the tower promptly. Watch HP reach 1 after one hit and 0 after the next. Coins should go from 90 to 60 to 70.
Wait after the enemy disappears. Coins must stay at 70 and base health at 5.
Restart without buying. The enemy should escape, leaving 90 coins and 4 base health.
hints: An if-else gives these two outcomes separate branches. Do not put the escape test after the entire if-else.
Once Game State becomes ready, the Stage stops sending movement and attack messages, but still sends Draw Shots to hide the last shot.

debuggingTips.symptom: Coins keep increasing after a defeat.
checks: Set Game State to ready in the defeat branch.
Keep the entire Enemy Step inside if Game State equals combat.

checkpoint.task: Test one defended run and one undefended run.
checkpoint.expectedResult: Defense ends with 70 coins and 5 health. No tower ends with 90 coins and 4 health.
completeWhen: Each enemy takes two hits.
Only the defeat awards coins.
Neither outcome repeats afterward.

steps.title: Checkpoint: A Reusable Attack
steps.explanation: You now have a working purchase, shot, and enemy. The next chapter will number more copies instead of inventing six different shooting scripts.
instructions: Check the Stage's complete loop below. Tower Step must finish before Enemy Step, followed by Draw Shots.
